previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ , a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder managed with a chronic Foley catheter, was admitted with acute right arm weakness and general malaise. Evaluation revealed a urinary tract infection with E. coli resistant to trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole but sensitive to ampicillin/sulbactam. He was treated with intravenous Unasyn and transitioned to oral Augmentin. His neurological symptoms improved with infection treatment. A Foley catheter change resolved associated hematuria. He was discharged home with services, instructions to complete antibiotics, discontinue Bactrim and methenamine hippurate temporarily, and follow up with urology and MS infusion clinic.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Other and unspecified Escherichia coli [E. coli]

Brief Hospital Course:
IMPRESSION: ___ with a PMH significant for multiple sclerosis 
(requires wheelchair) and neurogenic bladder (requiring chronic 
indwelling Foley catheterization), history of prior urinary 
tract infections (mildly-resistant organisms), prior alcohol 
abuse and history of depression presenting with gross hematuria 
following traumatic Foley placement with positive urinalysis and 
low-grade temperatures with chronic unintentional weight loss.

# ASYMPTOMATIC BACTERURIA - Given the patient's known MS and 
neurogenic bladder with chronic indwelling Foley needs, patient 
has a history of chronic, complicated UTIs. Urine cultures have 
speciated Pseudomonas, E.coli, Enterococcus with some evidence 
of prior resistance. Symptoms with UTI include fever and 
worsened coordination; he did not experience either leading up 
to admission. We initially empirically treated him with 
Meropenem IV given his prior sensitivities and awaited further 
growth in his urine sample before tailoring treatment. His Foley 
catheter was changed on admission. Given that the culture grew 
multiple species and that he did not have his usual symptoms, we 
chose not to treat this as an active infection.

# TRAUMATIC HEMATURIA - Presents with gross hematuria and 
evidence of urethral meatus bleeding following traumatic Foley 
replacement on ___ with home visiting nurse. Hematocrit 
39.7% and improved with normal platelets. No history of 
coagulopathy. No symptomatic bleeding concerns. No concern for 
Urology pathology given urodynamic studies and cystoscopy in 
___ without visualized concerns (only moderate debris and 
trabeculation). His hematocrit remained normal and his Foley bag 
yielded clear urine without clots on this admission. He had some 
urethral meatus crusted blood, but this was improving with time.

# CHRONIC UNINTENTIONAL WEIGHT LOSS - Evidence of unintentional 
weight loss (30-lbs) over several months and deconditioning 
noted in the setting of mild chronic anemia and chronic multiple 
sclerosis. No chills or nightsweats. No LAD on exam. Has not had 
age-appropriate screening. We employed a standard work-up for 
unintentional weight loss. TSH, CRP, ESR, CXR, LFTs, HbA1c and 
electrolytes were all reassuring. His albumin was also normal. 
This work-up can be continued as an outpatient. We suggest 
age-appropriate screening with DRE and PSA check, colonoscopy.

# MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS - Multiple sclerosis (clinically definite 
since ___ secondary progressive type with gait disorder, 
limited mobility to wheelchair) with neurogenic bladder issues. 
Has some issues MS symptoms and deficits exacerbated by 
infectious or metabolic derangements. Has visiting nurse to 
assist with home ADLs. Has required recent IV Methylprednisolone 
dosing (last on ___. He will continued his outpatient 
steroid infusions, as appropriate. No acute neurologic concerns 
on this admission.

# NEUROGENIC BLADDER, CHRONIC INDWELLING CATHETERIZATION NEEDS - 
Requires chronic indwelling catheter given neurogenic bladder 
issues from MS. ___ by Dr. ___ Urology. On ___, had 
urodynamic studies and Foley catheter changed. We continued his 
Foley catheterization; has deferred intermittent straight 
catheterization. We also continued his Oxybutynin 10 mg ER PO 
daily.

# DEPRESSION - No active symptoms. Remains on SSRI dosing. We 
continued Fluoxetine 20 mg PO BID.

# PRIOR ALCOHOL ABUSE - No evidence of active alcohol use; 
history of prior heavy use. Has been on Thiamine 100 mg PO 
daily.

# TOBACCO USE - Provided Nicotine patch 21 mg TD daily and 
encouraged smoking cessation. 

# HYPERLIPIDEMIA - We continued Ezetimibe 10 mg PO daily.

your urinary infection concerns. You had no fevers or white

the bacteria that grew in your urine cultures were most likely

Please call your doctor or go to the emergency department if:
* You experience new chest pain, pressure, squeezing or 
tightness.
* You develop new or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or 
wheezing.
* You are vomiting and cannot keep down fluids, or your 
medications.
* If you are getting dehydrated due to continued vomiting, 
diarrhea, or other reasons. Signs of dehydration include: dry 
mouth, rapid heartbeat, or feeling dizzy or faint when standing.
* You see blood or dark/black material when you vomit, or have a 
bowel movement.
* You experience burning when you urinate, have blood in your 
urine, or experience an unusual discharge.
* You have pain that is not improving within 12 hours or is not 
under control within 24 hours.

Fahrenheit or 38 degrees Celsius.
